summary.label: Decision
summary.text: How customers get their invoices into their accounting tool. PO, CTO, UX and Philosopher sat, two rounds.

summary.label: Consensus
summary.text: A CSV export first; a live sync waits for demand.

summary.label: Recommendation
summary.text: Build in-house on the PDF pipeline. **Accepts:** PDF pipeline debt, to make the 1 Dec closing.

decisions.title: Accounting export: build or buy?
detail: Three customers wait on an export to close their books
Invoices already render to PDF in `src/billing/pdf.ts`
decisions.why: Picks who we depend on for a feature customers pay for.
decisions.accepts: PDF pipeline debt, to make the 1 Dec closing

for.point: Unblocks the three customers waiting on the export before their closing.
Reuses the invoice model the PDF already reads; no new service to run.

against.point: Two PDF code paths to keep in sync until the pipeline is merged.
A file download is one more step than a sync the user never sees.

decisions.title: Where does the export code live?
detail: The PDF code sits in `src/billing/pdf.ts`; the web layer calls it
decisions.why: A folder convention later work builds on.

tradeoff.tech: One module owns invoices; keeps KS1
Billing would import the web layer

for.point: Keeps the dependency rule from the September billing split.

against.point: Nobody measured how often the web team touches billing.

decisions.title: Charge for the export?
detail: Two of the three waiting customers are on the Starter plan
Competitors include an export in every plan
decisions.why: Sets what customers pay for a feature they asked for.

tradeoff.business: No new revenue; keeps the three customers
About 1 k€/month; a new price to sell before 1 Dec

for.point: The three customers asked for it to close their books, not as an extra.

against.point: Nobody asked the other customers whether they would pay for it.

rejected.title: Live sync with each accounting tool
rejected.reason: Three integrations to run before one customer asked
